Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Priya Mehta (Vantage Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (VP Eng), Nora Lee (FinOps)

Summary:
- Renewal discussion for upcoming Jan 2027 renewal; customer exploring capacity uplift and adding EU + APAC regions; sizing and pricing to be updated.
- Need to validate latency/SLA in EU region and run benchmarks; security docs/KMS questions pending.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to send updated quote and schedule benchmarks; customer to confirm preferred contract term.

Topics:
- Current usage and burst patterns
- Dedicated capacity vs hosted scaling
- Regional deployment and data residency
- Contract term, pricing uplift, and discounts
- Security (SOC2/KMS) and procurement timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: All right, hey team, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I'm Lena from Redwood, Marco our solutions engineer is here. Priya, Carlos, Nora, you all there?
[00:08] Priya Mehta: Yep, here.
[00:10] Carlos Ruiz: Yep, hi.
[00:12] Nora Lee: Morning.
[00:14] Lena Park: Great. The agenda for today is pretty focused — renewal, capacity bump, adding EU and APAC regions, and any procurement questions. Sound good?
[00:20] Priya Mehta: Yep, that's exactly it. We're up for renewal in January and the team's forecasted growth means we need more dedicated capacity, especially in EU.
[00:28] Marco Silva: Cool. Can you remind us of your current footprint — tokens per day, peak concurrency, and any regional latency targets?
[00:35] Priya Mehta: So right now we're at about 40k tokens a day average, spikes to around 120k on promo days. Concurrency peaks maybe 35 concurrent requests. Latency — our SLA internal target is <200ms p95 for user-facing chat. EU target same but ideally <250ms.
[00:50] Marco Silva: Got it. On Redwood Dedicated we can guarantee throughput with reserved GPU pools; latency depends a bit on model and batch size but 200–250ms p95 is reasonable for our 7B/13B equivalents if you use shorter context.
[01:05] Carlos Ruiz: Quick question — we ran with hosted before; when you say dedicated, what's the typical uplift in cost and does that also include region placement?
[01:12] Lena Park: Good question. Dedicated is a reserved capacity price — there's a base monthly commit + per-token execution cost that tends to be lower unit-wise than burst on hosted. Region placement is configurable; there is usually a regional uplift for EU/APAC due to capacity footprint. We'll send a detailed quote but ballpark is a 20–35% uplift for dedicated vs hosted depending on commit term and model family.
[01:30] Nora Lee: When you say commit term — are there discounts for 24 vs 36 months? We're considering a longer term if the economics look good.
[01:36] Marco Silva: Yes, the longer the term the more capacity discount you can get; we can model 12, 24, 36 month options in the quote. Also if you commit to a certain throughput we can reserve nodes in EU which helps hit latency targets.
[01:48] Priya Mehta: On the technical side, we care about KV cache behavior and warm start. Our prompt lengths vary; can caching help with cost without hurting latency?
[01:55] Marco Silva: Absolutely — our runtime does prefix/KV caching and smart batching; it reduces per-token compute for repeated prefixes. For your workload (lots of repeated system prompts) that typically reduces cost by 10–25% depending on hit rate.
[02:08] Priya Mehta: Nice.
[02:10] Carlos Ruiz: Any gotchas on private deployments? We might need VPC peering for sensitive routes.
[02:16] Lena Park: For Vantage's compliance needs you can use Redwood Private or VPC mode — Private is the full control plane in your VPC, there are additional licensing/support fees. VPC peering + KMS/HSM integrations supported; we'll include the SOC2 + KMS docs.
[02:30] Nora Lee: Perfect. Procurement will want the SOC2 and an audit log sample.
[02:34] Lena Park: We'll attach those.
[02:36] Marco Silva: One note — our EU region currently runs on a slightly different instance mix; latency can be within 10–20% of NA for some models. We'll run a benchmark on EU+APAC to give empirical numbers.
[02:48] Priya Mehta: That would be really helpful. Any chance to test with our 90k token/day profile?
[02:53] Marco Silva: Yes that's feasible. We can run a targeted benchmark with your prompt set; we'll need a short sample dataset and a test API key.
[03:00] Priya Mehta: I'll share a sanitized set.
[03:03] Carlos Ruiz: About models — we currently run a 13B-ish open model. If we move to a quantized variant how much change in latency/cost should we expect?
[03:12] Marco Silva: Quantization typically reduces memory footprint and can speed inference slightly; cost reduces too. Expect 20–40% lower cost depending on quant level. There's a small potential accuracy delta which you should validate with your evals.
[03:25] Priya Mehta: We've got eval suites — we'll run those.
[03:28] Lena Park: Great. Switching to procurement timeline — Nora, what's your internal renewal timeline?
[03:32] Nora Lee: We need a signed SOW by January 15 to avoid service interruption; ideally we lock pricing by Dec 15 to hit our month-end approvals.
[03:41] Lena Park: OK, Dec 15 pricing lock is doable if we get the benchmark and final region list this week.
[03:49] Nora Lee: Good. Also be aware we might require EU data residency for a subset of endpoints — that's why the region details matter.
[03:56] Marco Silva: Understood. We'll note which endpoints can be pinned to EU nodes; Redwood routing supports policy-based routing and can fall back to NA if capacity constrained.
[04:06] Priya Mehta: Any issues with KMS integration? We use AWS KMS and a couple of HSM-backed keys for production.
[04:12] Marco Silva: We support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys; for Private deployments you can bring HSM. For hosted we do envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS where possible. We'll send the integration steps.
[04:23] Priya Mehta: Thanks.
[04:25] Lena Park: Let's talk numbers — baseline renewal has your current committed capacity. For a 2x bump in commit to handle bursts (targeting 80–100k tokens/day average) we can propose X GPU equivalent and show cost delta. Nora, is finance looking for an annual figure or monthly?
[04:40] Nora Lee: We prefer annualized with quarterly invoicing if possible. Also we need to see the breakouts: base commit, per-token overage, regional uplift, and any premium for Private.
[04:50] Lena Park: We'll format the quote that way.
[04:52] Carlos Ruiz: One more technical: how do model rollouts work across regions? If we push a new model version, can we control where it gets deployed?
[04:59] Marco Silva: Yes — rollouts can be regional and you can do canary percentages. We also support automatic fallback to compatible model variants if a region is constrained. There was a small ops note — sometimes model variant names get slightly different kernel selections per region but functionally the same.
[05:15] Priya Mehta: Sounds good.
[05:18] Lena Park: Okay, call to action — we'll: 1) send updated quote with 12/24/36 term options and regional pricing, 2) schedule benchmarks for EU/APAC with your sample prompts, 3) attach SOC2/KMS docs.
[05:30] Priya Mehta: That works. Anything else on your side, Carlos?
[05:33] Carlos Ruiz: Not now. We'll review the quote once we get it.
[05:36] Lena Park: Great. Marco, can you confirm availability for the benchmark next week?
[05:40] Marco Silva: Yes, I'm available Wed/Thu — we'll need about 2–3 hours of coordination and then 24–48 hours for runs and analysis.
[05:49] Priya Mehta: We'll aim for Wed.
[05:51] Lena Park: Perfect. Does anyone have any immediate blockers?
[05:55] Nora Lee: Just to note procurement will need a copy of the SAML/SSO integration guide too.
[05:59] Lena Park: We'll add that to the doc bundle.
[06:02] Priya Mehta: Quick question — we mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI earlier in our internal evaluation; how do you position Redwood compared to those?
[06:10] Marco Silva: Redwood is focused on production inference economics and operational controls — unified runtime, routing policies, and cost tools. Anthropic/OpenAI are model providers; Redwood layers on top for serving and hosting flexibility. Often customers use a mix — some traffic to hosted model APIs, some to Dedicated.
[06:26] Priya Mehta: Ok that matches our understanding.
[06:29] Lena Park: All right, unless there's anything else, we'll capture action items. Thanks everyone.
[06:33] Carlos Ruiz: Thanks.
[06:35] Nora Lee: Thanks, talk soon.
